264K likes, 6,252 comments - dougdoesdelicious on July 8, 2026: "Cheat sheet for how to win a 19-person one pot dish challenge on Food Network:

80/20 Hainanese Chicken and Rice (One Pot version):

Ingredients
2 chicken thighs (450 g)
2 tsp sesame oil (5 g)
¼ tsp salt (1.5 g)

Rice
1 cup jasmine rice (200 g)
6 clove garlic (15 g)
½ inch ginger (15 g)
3 green onions (45 g)
1 ¼ cup chicken broth (300 g)
1 tsp chicken bouillon powder (5 g)
½ tsp turmeric powder (1 g)

Ginger Scallion Sauce
½ inch ginger (15 g)
1 green onion (15 g)
1 tsp sesame oil (5 g)
salt (1g)
2 tbsp neutral oil (25 g)

Chili Garlic Sauce
6 clove garlic (15 g)
½ inch ginger (15 g)
2 tbsp sambal (25 g)
2 tbsp sriracha (25 g)
1 tbsp chicken broth (15 g)
1 tsp lime juice (5 g)
2 tsp sugar (10 g)

Toppings
1 cucumber (100 g)
cilantro 
green onion 

Directions
1. Place chicken thighs in a mixing bowl and season with sesame oil and salt.
2. Add jasmine rice, garlic, ginger, green onion, chicken bone broth, chicken bouillon, and turmeric powder into a pot. (No need to rinse the rice)
3. Place chicken thighs on top of the rice.
4. Get the pot up to a boil, then drop to a simmer. Cover with a lid and simmer for 20 minutes or until the water completely evaporates.
5. While your chicken and rice are cooking, prepare your sauces. We’ll start with the ginger scallion sauce. Sart by adding ginger, green onion and salt into a bowl.
6. Heat the sesame oil and neutral oil in a pan until hot. I usually heat the oil until I start to see the oil start to shimmer or produce the first whisp of smoke. Please watch over the oil while doing this step to avoid accidentally starting a fire.
7. Pour hot oil into the bowl with the rest of the ginger scallion sauce and mix.
8. To make the chili sauce, add garlic, ginger, sambal, sriracha, chicken broth, lime juice, and sugar into a bowl and mix.
9. After 20 minutes, take the chicken out and cut into slices or serve as is. Set the rice in the pot aside and let rest for another 10 minutes. Plate up a scoop of ginger garlic rice with chicken, the sauces, and optional toppings like green onion, cilantro, and / or cucumbers.

#foodnetwork #onepotmeal".

audio.transcript: This dish won first place in a 19 person one pot meal challenge on Food Network. This dish for me is packed with flavor, bursting with flavor, that doesn't even fit in this bowl. I'm struggling not to eat this whole thing. And when you walk away, I'm probably going to eat the rest. And this is how you can make it. It's my favorite 80/20 Hainenese chicken and rice recipe. It's one of the most saved recipes on my channel. I promise no matter how many times you make this, it'll always catch you by surprise. My original 80/20 recipe uses a rice cooker, but in a 40 minute challenge, I didn't want to risk being sent home on a rice cooker that I've never used before. So I adapted the recipe to use only a pot over the stove so I could have more control. But just as easy as the rice cooker recipe, you throw everything into the pot before laying the chicken thighs on top of the rice. Then you bring the pot to a boil, drop to a simmer and cover for 20 minutes. While the chicken and rice are simmering, you can prepare all the sauces. One of the things that was most surprising about competing on stage is how quickly time seems to evaporate when you're up there. A lot of my contestant friends said they just blacked out and I didn't understand what they meant until I came down to the kitchen. To sort myself from losing track of time, I had a two minute timer constantly running in the background to snap me back into reality. Speaking of which, after 20 minutes or once all the water in the pot has cooked off, take the pot off the heat and let the rice rest for about another five to 10 minutes. You can take out the chicken at this point to cut and prepare. That's it. That's all it takes. I'd still highly recommend the rice cooker version because it's as simple as pushing a button. But if you somehow find yourself without a pressure cooker or your in one, now you know you've got a round winning dish in your back pocket. Number 66. You're the winner of this round.
